cards.headline: Producer price inflation in Ghana rises to 4.8% in September 2026

pages.text: Producer Price Inflation (PPI) in Ghana rose to 4.8% in September 2026, an increase of 0.4 percentage points. According to the Ghana Statistical Service, the month-on-month PPI stood at 1.3%, down from 2.5% in August 2026. The PPI recovered strongly in early 2026, fell sharply in June, and subsequently rebounded. Within the Mining and Quarrying sector, which recorded the highest index levels during this period, the index rose from 360.5 to 380.4. The Extraction of Crude Oil and Natural Gas sub-sector recorded an inflation rate of 18.35, while Mining Support Service Activities recorded an inflation rate of 5.3%, down from 5.7% in August 2026. Conversely, inflation in the Mining of Metal Ores sub-sector fell by 1.9 percentage points, from -0.4% in August 2026 to -2.3% in September 2026.

The Manufacturing Index increased from 258.7 to 270.5. Within the Manufacturing sub-sector, eight of the 23 major groups recorded inflation rates above the sub-sector average of 4.6%. The Manufacture of leather and related products recorded the highest inflation rate at 15.8%, followed by the Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment, at 14.3%. In contrast, the Manufacture of other non-metallic mineral products recorded deflation of 1.1 percent. Additionally, the Electricity, Gas, Steam and Air Conditioning Supply Index rose from 218.5 to 239.8.

cards.headline: Bank credit remains concentrated in Dhaka and Chattogram divisions of Bangladesh

pages.text: According to Bangladesh Bank data, lending remains heavily concentrated in the Dhaka and Chattogram divisions, which serve as the country's primary commercial and industrial centers. During the April-June quarter of 2026, these two divisions accounted for approximately three-quarters of the nation's total bank loans and advances. This concentration leaves regions most exposed to cyclones, floods, salinity, and river erosion receiving only a small share of bank credit, raising questions regarding whether formal financing is reaching communities attempting to adapt to climate change. In the Shyamnagar area of Satkhira, a region highly vulnerable to climate change, Saiful Gazi, a 34-year-old fish business owner, reported difficulty securing institutional financing. Gazi, who supports a family of four and survived Cyclone Aila on May 25, 2009, stated that a recent application for a private bank loan to expand his business was rejected due to insufficient documentation and a lack of collateral. He reported being compelled to use a high-interest loan from a local NGO to maintain his operations.

cards.headline: Ghana High Commission attributes South Africa evacuation data discrepancies to clerical errors

pages.text: The Ghana High Commission in Pretoria issued a press statement on October 19, 2026, addressing reports of data discrepancies during a government evacuation exercise in South Africa. The High Commission clarified that clerical errors occurred during the transcription of passport details by officials, rather than indicating falsified identities. These errors involved 15 individuals out of the 1,964 Ghanaians evacuated, specifically regarding reports that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs paid reintegration and transportation allowances to persons with dates of birth recorded in the future. The High Commission stated that the dates interpreted as future dates of birth were actually passport expiry dates. The institution maintained that these errors do not invalidate the identities of the evacuees or their receipt of approved allowances, noting that such mistakes can occur during the sudden evacuation of thousands of citizens in emergency circumstances.

To provide transparency, the High Commission released verified details for the 15 affected individuals, including names, dates of birth, occupations, passport numbers, and expiry dates. The listed individuals include James Akoto Baffour, Precious Sekyiwaa, Philip Oduro, Victoria Eduaquah, Prince Obeng Boateng, Ebenezer Losu, Akua Brifoh, Philimon Opoku Nsiah, Rebecca Agyiwaa Opoku, Emmanuel Ampomah, Rose Pokua, Thomas Nkrumah, Rita Acouah, Rashid Abubakar, and David Botwey. cards.headline: Alberta voters reject proposal to begin legal process for potential separation from Canada

pages.text: Voters in Alberta, Canada, overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin a legal process that could lead to a second vote on independence on October 19, 2026. According to unofficial results from Elections Alberta, with more than 1.5 million votes counted, 76% supported remaining in Canada, while approximately 24% backed beginning a process toward separation. The ballot question was one of 10 presented to Albertans, with others covering healthcare, education, immigration, and constitutional powers. The separation question specifically addressed whether to remain in Canada or initiate a legal process that could eventually lead to a second vote on independence. Results were delayed by more than two hours due to issues at roughly 100 of the 1,400 polling stations across the province.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, described the result as a choice for unity. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith also welcomed the early results, stating they showed support for a stronger Alberta within a united Canada. Keith Wilson, a leader of the separatist movement, noted that while final results were not yet in, the numbers suggested at least a quarter of Albertans feel the province needs to be treated better. The Canadian Broadcasting Corp. projected victory for the side favoring remaining in Canada after approximately 1.2 million votes were counted.

cards.headline: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrives in India for trade and energy talks

pages.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday to participate in negotiations regarding defense cooperation, energy security, and trade tariffs. Beginning his two-day trip in Mumbai, Rubio was received by Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar. Jaishankar stated that the two officials shared views on advancing ties in technology, defense, energy, trade, and people-to-people relations. Rubio told reporters in Mumbai that the US is “very close” to finalizing the deal, noting that only a small number of items remain to be wrapped up. This marks Rubio's second trip to India this year, following a visit to Uzbekistan.

During the visit, Rubio is scheduled to visit the Reliance Industries crude oil refining complex in Jamnagar on October 14, 2026. The facility, owned by Mukesh Ambani, is the world’s largest crude oil refining complex. Addressing India's role in the energy sector, Rubio described the country as a “refining superpower” with the capability to refine heavy crude. He noted that as more Venezuelan oil becomes available, India has the capacity to process it. Rubio stated that the US has discussed Venezuela and other countries with India, adding that it is in the interest of the US to have allies with diverse energy portfolios. This comes as the US administration has managed Venezuela's petroleum reserves since the ousting of former President Nicolas Maduro in January.

cards.headline: Houthi ballistic missile attack kills at least 53 in Yemen training camp

pages.text: At least 53 people were killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on the al-Alam training camp for Yemeni government security forces in the southern Shabwa province. According to The Guardian World, this represents the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September. More than 200 others, described as mostly young recruits, were reportedly injured in the strike on the police and army training camp located in the Jardan district. The injured were transported to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were issued. An inquiry is planned to determine how the troops were left exposed to the attack. This follows a mid-September push by the Houthi group along the Red Sea coast toward the Bab al-Mandab waterway. Separately, a Saudi airstrike on October 18, 2026, killed nine people, including five children and two women.

Rashad al-Alimi, the president of the UN-recognised government, stated that those killed on Monday were new recruits and vowed an immediate hard response. Al-Alimi characterized the incident as a terrorist attack and contacted UN secretary general António Guterres to request that the Houthis be classified as a foreign terrorist organisation. The Shabwa provincial authority described the targeting of recruits as a military escalation and an assault on provincial security. Awad bin al-Wazir, the governor of Shabwa, visited the wounded and called for additional air defences, noting that troops are currently fighting across six fronts. While reliable assessments of the total death toll from fighting over the last month are difficult to gather, reports suggest the number is running into the many thousands.

cards.headline: Bangladesh state minister says education reforms must extend beyond curriculum

pages.text: On October 19, 2026, the State Minister for Primary and Mass Education in Bangladesh, Bobby Hajjaj, stated that curriculum reforms alone would not improve primary education unless teacher training, school supervision, infrastructure, and technology are addressed together. Speaking at a dialogue organized by the ministry, the Directorate of Primary Education (DPE), and Unicef, Hajjaj noted that a proposed curriculum would place greater emphasis on English, mathematics, Bangla, digital content, practical activities, and play-based learning. The ministry plans to test teaching materials and assessments in 2027, with a revised curriculum scheduled for introduction in 2028. Additionally, a 12-month practical learning programme has been proposed to cover topics such as child protection, road safety, hygiene, nutrition, digital safety, and environmental protection. A teacher policy is also being prepared to cover recruitment, training, postings, professional development, and evaluation, with Hajjaj stressing that teachers should receive training before entering classrooms. Planning State Minister Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki added that improving the professional skills, status, and salaries of teachers is essential to reducing dropouts and raising education quality.

The ministry presented findings from consultations held between July 26 and September 10 involving more than 3,200 participants across eight divisions. The ministry also proposed common minimum standards for primary schools, including equal instruction time for single- and double-shift schools, with annual teaching hours ranging from 750 for Class I to 900 for Class V, subject to approval. Survey data presented during the dialogue included responses from 1,036 monitoring officials, which found that 86.3 percent could visit no more than 10 schools per month, while 58.2 percent supervised more than 50 schools each. A separate survey of 580 officials found that 84.3 percent wanted duplicate or lengthy reporting requirements reduced. These figures reflect the responses of officials rather than verified inspection records.

cards.headline: Ghanaian government declines most Constitutional Review Committee recommendations on natural resources and environment

pages.text: Following the publication of a Government Position Paper regarding the final recommendations of the Constitution Review Committee (CRC), the government of Ghana has declined substantially all proposals concerning lands, natural resources, and environmental thematic areas. The CRC had proposed several reforms, including a clearer public trust framework for natural resources, stronger parliamentary oversight of resource transactions, basic principles for natural resource governance, and improved institutional coordination. Other CRC proposals included the constitutional recognition of ocean governance and the blue economy, the creation of an offence of ecocide, and a guaranteed share of mineral revenue for mining communities. cards.headline: Community organizers hold civic engagement fair in Toronto to encourage voter participation

pages.text: Community organizers held a non-partisan fair at the Lawrence Heights Community Centre in Toronto to raise civic engagement and encourage residents to vote in the Oct. 26 municipal election. Organized by the North York Harvest Food Bank, the event included participation from Voice the Vote, a joint initiative by United Way Greater Toronto and Toronto Metropolitan University’s Democratic Engagement Exchange. During the event, Jonathan Dong distributed election handbooks and spoke about the importance of participating in the democratic process. This effort follows previous municipal elections in the city that saw what observers described as a downward trend in voter participation. In the 2023 mayoral byelection won by Olivia Chow, 37 per cent of eligible voters participated, while turnout was less than 30 per cent in the 2022 municipal election and approximately 41 per cent in 2018. Data from the Association of Municipalities of Ontario indicated that across the province, overall voter turnout was nearly 33 per cent in the 2022 municipal elections and roughly 38 per cent in 2018. However, turnout at Toronto's advance polls for the upcoming election was reported as more than 222,000 people, the highest number in more than a decade.

cards.headline: Syrian Kurds protest introduction of Arabic-language instruction in northeastern schools

pages.text: Hundreds of Syrian Kurds protested across northeastern Syria last month to demand that Kurdish remains the primary language of instruction in schools, according to reporting by Syria Direct. The protests follow a government decision to begin teaching certain courses in Arabic, a move that residents say surprised them because previous government statements had not mentioned teaching in Arabic. Protesters expressed fears that the decision could lead to educational setbacks and the erosion of Kurdish identity. On October 19, 2026, residents stated that gains made by Kurds under the Kurdish-led Autonomous Administration are unraveling. This development is described as a flashpoint testing the integration between the Syrian government and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), which officially announced its dissolution in August.

In Qamishli, students, parents, and residents gathered at the March 12 Stadium, a site associated with the start of the 'Kurdish Intifada' after dozens of Kurds were killed by security forces and allied tribal fighters during a football match in 2004. The current dispute follows a January decree by Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa recognizing Kurdish linguistic and cultural rights and designating Kurdish as a national language. Additionally, last March, the Ministry of Education had called on Kurdish language specialists and educators to develop a Kurdish language curriculum. Despite these actions, Kurdish students and parents reported being shocked to find Arabic being used as a primary language of instruction when the school year began last month.

cards.headline: Global food inflation expected to accelerate and persist through 2027

pages.text: Global food inflation is projected to accelerate in the coming months and continue into 2027 due to supply shocks including El Nino-driven droughts and war-related shipping disruptions. Maximo Torero, chief economist at the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), stated that the system is under considerable pressure and that impacts may increase toward the end of this year, the beginning of next year, and potentially throughout next year. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded commodities, averaged 136 points in September, marking its highest reading since November 2022. According to the World Bank, food prices in the September quarter outpaced headline inflation in 22 percent of the 150 countries analyzed, an increase from 14 percent in the previous quarter.

Supply disruptions have impacted various commodities and regions. Attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure have disrupted wheat shipments, affecting importers such as Egypt and Indonesia, while insecurity in the Red Sea has diverted vessels onto longer routes around Africa. Additionally, the US-Israeli war on Iran has raised fuel prices and disrupted fertilizer exports through the Strait of Hormuz. Environmental factors have also contributed to price increases, including the weakest monsoon in over a decade in India and dry El Nino weather in India and Southeast Asia. Specific price impacts include record high rice prices in Indonesia, a 25 percent increase in the cost of bread in Egypt, and all-time high sugar prices in India. The rising costs are noted to hit the world's poorest consumers hardest in low- and middle-income countries across West Asia, North Africa, and Asia.

Mirella Riccardi, a mental health and psychosocial support worker for MSF, stated that internal conflict and war make already fragile communities more vulnerable, describing Ebola as an additional element that fragilizes mental health conditions. At a mental health treatment center in Bunia, one patient reported feeling isolated after losing two close relatives and three extended family members to the disease, noting that neighbors are often afraid to approach those affected. cards.headline: Ebola cases in Kenya emerge amid controversy over US-led quarantine center

pages.text: An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, marking the country’s first cluster of cases of the virus. This occurs as the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history has sickened more than 9,000 people and killed more than 4,300 in the region, according to reporting by The Guardian World. The emergence of these cases follows the establishment of a controversial US-led quarantine center at Kenya’s Laikipia airbase, intended for Americans returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The center has faced local opposition and protests, leading a Kenyan court to order a halt to its operations. Allan Maleche, executive director of the Kenya Legal & Ethical Issues Network on HIV and Aids (Kelin), stated that many Kenyans were concerned by a lack of information regarding why the facility was being set up and who would use it. Maleche noted that Kenyans have been cautious regarding government information about Ebola, and added that litigation regarding the center is expected to be decided in November.

The situation highlights a diminished role by the United States in the regional Ebola outbreak, characterized by the creation of the Laikipia airbase center, the banning of travelers from certain countries, and a withdrawal from the World Health Organization (WHO) alongside sweeping funding cuts. These actions have been linked to a reduced ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and an increase in mistrust. Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the pandemic center at Brown University school of public health, questioned if the center remains a viable solution for the US, asking if the arrangement poses an undue burden on the Kenyan government and whether it is the safest location for Americans. Additionally, some Americans have pushed back against the center, questioning whether the US possesses the legal authority to quarantine its citizens on foreign soil and prevent their return home.

cards.headline: Donald Trump endorses Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's parliamentary election

pages.text: US President Donald Trump issued a complete and total endorsement of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, prior to Israel's parliamentary election scheduled for October 27. In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump described Netanyahu as a partner the United States demands of Israel and a leader who has been strong, brave, and brilliant in the face of opposition. Trump also characterized Netanyahu as a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and suggested that if anyone other than Netanyahu were re-elected, the United States would have to handle the work against Iran itself, which he stated he is not inclined to do. Trump further noted that the US would be alone in the war against Iran if Netanyahu were not re-elected, referencing the labeling of the US and Israel as “the big and small Satans” by Iran's Revolutionary Guards. The endorsement comes less than two weeks before the first Israeli vote since the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack. While polls suggest the election is a tight race, some indicate that neither Netanyahu nor the opposition may secure the 61 seats required to form a coalition. Opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for the October 7 attack after allegedly ignoring warnings.

Netanyahu thanked Trump for his support on Sunday, stating, “Together we will complete the mission!” In a video released by his Likud party, Netanyahu touted his relationship with the US president, claiming that together they had “crushed Iran” and stating that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to eliminate the Iranian threat within two years or sooner. Netanyahu previously described Trump in August as one of the greatest friends Israel has had in the White House. The two leaders have worked together on multi-front wars following the October 7 attack, including actions involving Iran. Trump joined Netanyahu in a US-Israeli attack on Iran in late February, though he agreed to a ceasefire in April following US public opposition to the war, which had caused oil prices to spiral. cards.headline: Growing fears in Europe regarding the spillover of Russia’s war in Ukraine

pages.text: European nations have expressed growing fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spread regionally and spill over into neighboring NATO members. Some countries argue the conflict has already expanded, citing instances of sabotage, cyberattacks, and drone incursions. European officials state that Moscow is targeting allies of Ukraine to facilitate intimidation, though the Kremlin denies these accusations. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski has warned that Europe must be prepared to respond robustly to Russia’s hybrid attacks. Poland, which borders Ukraine, serves as a NATO logistics hub for both military and civilian support to its neighbor. The International Centre for Counterterrorism has identified Poland as the primary focus of Russia’s sabotage campaign in Europe. Emad Al-Din Hamad, the director general of Syrian Post, stated that the organization resumed deliveries of parcels and goods between provinces in May after a gap of more than 10 years. The service currently accepts shipments weighing up to 30 kilograms through central post offices, with plans to gradually extend the network of offices. Since March, the organization has also expanded a fleet of mobile offices designed to serve remote towns, sparsely populated areas, and locations where services were temporarily interrupted by technical problems. These mobile offices provide services including pension payments, postal money transfers, and transactions using the Sham Cash digital-payment and mobile transfer application.

Regarding international operations, Hamad said the international postal exchange office at Damascus International Airport has been repaired and returned to use in cooperation with Syrian Airlines, customs authorities, and the Universal Postal Union. International parcel services resumed on July 1, and the first incoming parcel from Jordan arrived on July 5. On October 1, the organization launched a service for sending parcels to worldwide destinations through the Universal Postal Union’s network. To expand cross-border e-commerce, Syrian Post reported it is working with Qatar Post and Qatar Airways to develop international mail transportation. The organization is also exploring Qatar Post’s “Connected” platform to facilitate purchases from online marketplaces in the US and Europe, and has held talks with Turkish Post regarding the connection of local delivery services with Turkish e-commerce platforms. Over the past year, Syrian Post has opened or reactivated 164 postal offices, consisting of 111 reactivated locations and 53 new locations. Hamad added that the organization is preparing to launch international money transfers.

cards.headline: University of Ghana and KNUST postpone reopening due to administrator strike

pages.text: The University of Ghana (UG) and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Ghana have postponed their reopening dates indefinitely. The decision follows a strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA), which has created uncertainty regarding the return of university administrators to their offices. According to a statement issued on October 10, 2026, signed by Professor Gordon A. Awandare, the Pro Vice-Chancellor, Academic and Student Affairs, the management of UG announced the postponement of the university's reopening, which had been scheduled for October 12, 2026. KNUST had scheduled its reopening for the day following the statement's issuance. The GAUA strike involves senior administrative staff, including registrars, admission officers, finance officers, and student affairs officers. The association has laid down its tools over unresolved concerns regarding allowances, conditions of service, and what it describes as unfair treatment compared to other staff categories within the universities. The strike has halted critical operations, including admissions, academic records management, registration, accommodation allocation, payroll management, accounting, human resources, corporate affairs, and related clerical work.

cards.headline: Opposition leaders lead march to Supreme Court in Delhi, India, to demand election chief's resignation

pages.text: Opposition leaders and student groups led a procession through Delhi on Monday to the Indian Supreme Court to submit a petition calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The march followed weekend unrest in the capital, during which thousands of people were detained and harassed by police while attempting to protest alongside the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups. To manage the demonstrations, police closed several metro stations in central Delhi and established barricades that prevented thousands of protesters from getting within 600m of the Supreme Court, forcing many to turn back. However, lawyers confirmed they submitted a petition on behalf of Rahul Gandhi, the leader of India’s opposition alliance, and by late evening, Gandhi reached the court gates after breaking through the barricades. Chief Justice Surya Kant responded to the petition by stating the matter is sub judice but assured that such petitions would be heard at the earliest possible opportunity in accordance with the law. 130 million names have been deleted from voter lists since last year as part of a special intensive revision (SIR) to verify and “purify” electoral rolls. Opposition parties and civil society groups allege that Kumar implemented this revision to help entrench the power of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), claiming Muslim voters and other minorities have been disproportionately affected. The Election Commission has denied favoring any party, stating that wrongly deleted voters can re-enroll, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by questioning electoral processes. During a press conference before the march, Gandhi accused the government of using the commission to commit “vote chori” (cheating) and referred to Kumar as a “thief.”

cards.headline: Bangladesh government transfers unused Sonali Bag machinery to MBSTU

pages.text: The government of Bangladesh has transferred unused machinery from the Sonali Bag project to Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University (MBSTU) to support research into jute-based technologies and prevent the deterioration of public assets. State Minister for Textiles and Jute Shariful Alam handed the machinery over to the university’s vice-chancellor following the signing of a memorandum of understanding on October 8 between the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC), the Bangladesh Climate Change Trust, and the university. The Sonali Bag project, which aimed to create a biodegradable alternative to plastic using jute cellulose, was scrapped on April 29, 2025, following a recommendation from a technical committee, according to a BJMC statement sent to The Daily Star. The Tk 100 crore project was deemed commercially unviable because production costs could not be reduced to acceptable levels; the statement noted that each bag would need to sell for Tk 25-40 to cover costs. Additionally, an 11-member committee found that producing five tonnes of Sonali bags required 40 tonnes of chemicals, which raised environmental concerns. Shariful Alam stated that the machinery will be used to support research into jute cellulose and eco-friendly products, noting that the facilities will be accessible to private researchers and may be used by the ministry for research and training. The minister added that the government is working with the environment ministry and other institutions to develop alternatives to polythene bags, suggesting that reusable jute bags could offer long-term savings despite higher initial costs.

cards.headline: Russia pledges additional humanitarian aid to Lebanon and calls for immediate ceasefire

pages.text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated on Monday that Moscow will send additional humanitarian aid to Lebanon and called for an immediate ceasefire amid ongoing Israeli military operations. Speaking in Moscow following talks with Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Raji, Lavrov reaffirmed Russia’s support for the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of Lebanon, according to reporting by Arab News citing the Russian state news agency TASS. Lavrov noted that almost 1 million Lebanese citizens have been seriously affected and described the humanitarian situation in the country as remaining tense. Russia previously sent humanitarian aid to Lebanon in April and is planning further deliveries.

Lavrov welcomed the commencement of direct, US-mediated talks between Israel and Lebanon but asserted that the conflict must transition toward a political and diplomatic settlement. He called for the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701, which facilitated the end of the 2006 war between Israel and Hezbollah. The resolution mandates a cessation of hostilities, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon as the Lebanese army deploys, and maintains an area between the Israeli border and the Litani River free of unauthorized weapons. Lavrov stated that the Israeli military was violating international law and fueling escalation. According to Lebanon’s Health Ministry, at least 4,386 people have been killed and 12,424 wounded since March 2.

cards.headline: Cyber-attack forces temperatures in several French supermarket refrigerators to 50C

pages.text: An unprecedented cyber-attack has targeted connected refrigeration systems at several major food retailers across France, forcing temperatures in some units up to 50C (120F). The Paris prosecutor’s office stated on Monday that the large-scale attack is affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers, reporting damage that includes food losses and fires. 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, while more than 100 supermarkets from Coopérative U were targeted. A spokesperson for Coopérative U stated the chain had thrown away all food to avoid health risks. Additionally, BFM TV reported that E.Leclerc, France’s largest supermarket chain, was also affected by hackers remotely triggering forced defrosting in numerous stores. Other major retailers, including Carrefour and Monoprix, were also hit. 100 additional Coopérative U shops were reportedly disconnected from the internet to prevent further targeting. While the full scale is unclear, figures from individual chains suggest approximately 400 stores were affected out of roughly 15,000 in France. The attack may not have been confined to France, and authorities are coordinating with European counterparts as other countries may be affected. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed the national cybersecurity agency, ANSSI, to investigate. The attack reportedly targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss, which allows retailers to manage cold units remotely. Danfoss stated the affected units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a previously identified risk, adding that the firm had long advised businesses to keep supported systems up to date. Dominique Schelcher, chief executive of Coopérative U, described the targeting of equipment essential to the food supply as an act of extreme gravity and unprecedented.

pages.text: A Dhaka court on October 11, 2026, placed four individuals on remand following their alleged involvement in an attempt to deface a mural of Nobel laureate poet Rabindranath Tagore in Segunbagicha, Dhaka. Additional Public Prosecutor Muhammad Shamsud Doha Sumon stated the order followed a 10-day remand prayer from police.  The case was filed at Shahbagh Police Station involving allegations of criminal conspiracy, inciting enmity between classes, and inciting religious hatred. Police reports allege that on October 9, Ayas announced intentions to erase the mural by whitewashing it. On October 10, the group reportedly went to the site, where Rimi allegedly smeared black ink over the mural of Tagore and attempted to incite religious hatred related to the upcoming Durga Puja. The mural was part of a series of portraits of 10 prominent cultural figures painted on a boundary wall after the Dhaka South City Corporation cleared the adjacent footpath of encroachments on October 5.

cards.headline: Cleveland-Cliffs CEO prepared to fight Canadian government in court over Stelco layoffs

pages.text: Lourenco Goncalves, CEO of the American company Cleveland-Cliffs, stated on Sunday that he is prepared to fight the Canadian government in court to preserve plans to lay off hundreds of workers at Hamilton-based steelmaker Stelco. Speaking on CBC's Rosemary Barton Live, Goncalves disputed claims by the Canadian government that the company is violating binding employment commitments made under the Investment Canada Act during its 2024 purchase of Stelco. Goncalves argued that there is no provision in the contract requiring the company to maintain specific employment levels every day throughout the five-year period through 2029. He stated, “If that was an imposition of the Canadian government, I would not have accepted.”

The dispute follows an ultimatum issued last week by Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, who demanded the company share a plan to save up to 500 jobs that could be impacted at the Hamilton plant or face potential legal action. Joly asserted that the purchase included undertakings to continue employing at least the same number of unionized employees and the vast majority of non-unionized employees as were employed when the transaction was announced. Prime Minister Mark Carney also stated last week that Ottawa would use all available powers to pursue the Ohio-based company to the “fullest extent of the law.”

Stelco Inc. responded to Joly in a letter, stating the company will proceed with the layoffs and calling the government's characterization of a breach of undertakings “false.” Goncalves reiterated the company's position that the layoffs are a temporary measure intended to last until Canada and the U.S. reach a trade agreement, at which point jobs would be restored. While Stelco has cited U.S. President Donald Trump's 50 per cent tariffs as a factor in its economic struggles, Goncalves voiced support for those tariffs and noted he is open to selling the company.

cards.headline: Nuclear war and malicious AI use pose extinction risks by 2100, Lancet assessment finds

pages.text: A new global risk assessment by The Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health identifies nuclear conflict and the malicious use of artificial intelligence as threats that could lead to human extinction within the next 75 years. The report states that nuclear conflict could potentially end humanity by injecting particles into the upper atmosphere to block sunlight and cause famine, while AI could be used to create biological weapons. Although the commission noted the likelihood of these specific events remains low, an accompanying editorial warned that their realization would inflict an apocalypse on humanity. 17 catastrophic threats to human health were identified by the commission, all of which were noted to have a “realistic route to act” upon. The commission modeled these threats based on disability-adjusted life years (Dalys), measuring potential years of healthy life lost due to sickness, disability, or early death. Other major catastrophic threats identified as potentially causing more than 1bn cumulative Dalys include climate breakdown, air pollution, antimicrobial resistance, childhood malnutrition, conventional conflict, declining overseas aid, high alcohol use, high blood pressure, income inequality, low educational attainment, naturally occurring pandemics, obesity, poor mental health, smoking, and unhealthy ageing.

cards.headline: Bangladesh Home Minister to skip BIMSTEC ministerial meeting in Delhi

pages.text: Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed will not attend the first-ever meeting of home ministers from the seven-nation Bay of Bengal regional bloc, BIMSTEC, scheduled for October 6, 2026, in New Delhi, India. BIMSTEC Secretary General Indra Mani Pandey confirmed to Prothom Alo that while home ministers and state ministers from the other six member countries will participate, Bangladesh will be represented by a four-member delegation led by Home Ministry Senior Secretary Monzur Morshed Chowdhury. The decision was reflected in a diplomatic letter from the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs sent to the BIMSTEC Secretariat on October 4, which listed the delegation for meetings on October 12 and 13 but excluded the home minister's name. Senior government officials, speaking anonymously, told Prothom Alo the decision was made in the context of ongoing strain in bilateral relations with India. This follows a September incident where Prime Minister Tarique Rahman did not attend a BRICS summit outreach session in Delhi; the Bangladesh government clarified that the invitation had been extended to him as the BIMSTEC chair rather than as Prime Minister.

The upcoming ministerial meeting in Delhi is expected to be chaired by Indian Home Minister Amit Shah, with a preceding meeting of senior home ministry officials on October 12 to be conducted by India's Home Secretary, Govind Mohan. Scheduled participants from other member states include Bhutan's Home Minister Lungten Dorji, Myanmar's Home Minister General Ko Ko Oo, Nepal's Home Minister Sudan Gurung, Sri Lanka's Home Minister Chandana Aberathne, and Thailand's Deputy Minister of Interior Songsak Thongsri. According to relevant sources, the meeting will focus on strengthening regional cooperation to combat terrorism and cross-border crime. Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of BIMSTEC in April 2025. The seven-member bloc, which aims to bridge cooperation between South and South-East Asia, includes Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan.

cards.headline: Developments in the Gaza Strip one year after ceasefire implementation

pages.text: One year after a ceasefire deal came into effect in the Gaza Strip, the territory lacks the promised international peacekeeping force and reconstruction efforts, according to reporting by NPR World. The deal followed efforts by President Donald Trump to push Israel to agree to a ceasefire and Hamas to release remaining Israeli hostages. While bombings have slowed during the ceasefire, Israel has continued targeting Hamas, and Gaza's Health Ministry reports that these attacks have killed more than 1,400 Palestinians over the past year, including nearly 500 women and children. NPR reporter Anas Baba has documented moments of respite and grief throughout the 12-month period, including a Palestinian mother mourning her son at Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City following an Israeli airstrike that occurred just over a month into the ceasefire.

The Israeli military has expanded its control to approximately 70% of Gaza, a development that has squeezed more than 2 million Palestinians toward the edge of the sea. Despite these conditions, increased food entry has helped reverse starvation across the territory, allowing residents to recover from what U.N.-backed experts declared was a famine in the north of Gaza last year.

cards.headline: French archaeologist documents historic civilizations in AlUla, Saudi Arabia

pages.text: Laila Nehmé, a French archaeologist and research fellow with the French National Centre for Scientific Research, has been documenting the historic civilizations of AlUla, Saudi Arabia, since 2002. Working in cooperation with the Saudi Ministry of Culture, Nehmé specializes in the Nabataeans, an ancient Arab people, and the science of ancient writings known as epigraphy. Her research includes the study of Nabataean Aramaic, the language and script used by the Nabataeans for inscriptions on stone and papyri. Prior to her work in AlUla, Nehmé worked in Syria and at the ancient city of Petra in Jordan during the late 1980s and 1990s. According to Nehmé, the AlUla region contains heritage dating from the Paleolithic period approximately 200,000 years ago through to the 1980s, featuring sandstone cliff inscriptions in various scripts and rock art depicting human figures, cattle, and camels.

Nehmé reported to Arab News that excavations at the Hegra site, also known as Madain Salih or Al-Hijir, have yielded dozens of skeletons from several monumental tombs. She noted that some remains were remarkably well preserved due to the extremely dry climate and low humidity, with some skulls retaining hair, traces of skin along the spine, and fragments of leather or textile shrouds.

cards.headline: Police in Khulna, Bangladesh, instructed not to travel alone at night

pages.text: Police in the Khulna district of Bangladesh have been instructed not to travel alone at night following a knife attack that seriously injured a police inspector in Khulna city. The directive was issued in an official letter signed by the superintendent of police of the District Special Branch (DSB) on the night of October 9, 2026. The letter noted that special operations are underway in the Rupsa, Terokhada, Dighalia, and Batiaghata police station areas in response to the current law and order situation and several recent incidents, including attacks by criminals on law enforcement personnel. Unit in-charges were directed to take necessary measures to ensure the personal safety of personnel engaged in special operations and other duties. Copies of the directive were sent to all relevant offices and police stations under the district police. Khulna Superintendent of Police Sarker Omar Faruk told Prothom Alo that the restriction was imposed to prevent police personnel from falling victim to muggers while returning home after duty. When asked if the directive suggested police insecurity, Faruk stated the internal letter's main purpose is to ensure no personnel fall victim to muggers. The instruction follows an incident on October 9, 2026, at approximately 2:30 a.m., when 43-year-old Police Inspector Shah Alam was attacked by muggers in front of Khulna Collegiate School on Khan Jahan Ali Road. According to police sources, Alam was traveling by rickshaw in plain clothes after conducting a special operation in Rupsa upazila when three muggers intercepted him and attempted to snatch his money and mobile phones. When he resisted, the attackers struck both his wrists with a sharp machete. Alam was rescued by police and taken to a hospital, but as his condition deteriorated, he was transferred to a private hospital in Dhaka, where he remains under treatment in critical condition.

cards.headline: UK-Ghana Trade Resource Centre launched at 2026 investment summit

pages.text: The UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce (UKGCC), in partnership with the UK-Ghana Jobs and Economic Transformation (JET) Programme, has launched the UK-Ghana Trade Resource Centre. The launch was a major outcome of the UK-Ghana Trade & Investment Summit 2026, a three-day event involving government leaders, investors, and business executives under the theme, “A Decade of Trust, A Future Always On: Scaling the UK-Ghana Growth Partnership.” The Centre is designed as a market-access platform to help businesses identify opportunities, navigate export requirements, and build commercial partnerships between Ghana and the United Kingdom. Total bilateral trade between the two nations reached approximately £1.6 billion in the year to Q1 2026, though officials noted significant untapped opportunities remain for businesses in both countries. Adjoba Kyiamah, the Executive Director of the UKGCC, stated the Centre is a step toward addressing information and market-access challenges for businesses seeking to trade between the two nations. The platform aims to support firms in taking advantage of the UK-Ghana Trade Partnership Agreement (TPA) by providing guidance, market intelligence, and trade facilitation services.

The Trade Resource Centre will provide specific services for different business types. For export-ready Ghanaian businesses, the Centre is intended to offer market-specific guidance, export readiness support, referrals to technical expertise, and connections to British buyers and commercial networks. It will also work with partners to identify firms and facilitate business matchmaking. For importers and UK businesses looking to source from Ghana, the Centre will provide access to industry networks, partner referrals, and commercial linkage support to improve trade flows. cards.headline: Ashaiman Municipal Assembly lobbies for completion of storm-drain project in Ghana

pages.text: The Ashaiman Municipal Assembly in Ghana is appealing to authorities, including the Hydrological Services Agency, to complete a storm-drain project at the Gbemi Stream to mitigate flood risks. Freeman Tsekpo, the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), stated that funding is the primary obstacle to finishing the construction. According to the Assembly, only approximately 150 metres of the planned storm drain approaching the Starlight Bridge has been completed since work began following the construction of the bridge in 2020, leaving a critical section of the watercourse unconstructed. The Assembly noted that periodic desilting of the existing drain does not provide a permanent solution to the municipality's flooding challenges. Ashaiman has experienced major flooding in 2010, with further incidents reported in 2018 and 2024. Mr. Tsekpo noted that extensive dredging and desilting at the Ajei Kojo underbridge helped prevent major flooding during heavy rains in 2025 and 2026, but emphasized that such measures cannot replace a properly engineered storm-drain system.

The Gbemi Stream also faces challenges from indiscriminate dumping. During a recent Municipal Assembly clean-up exercise, workers and machines were deployed to remove refuse from the watercourse. Mr. Tsekpo reported that residents living along the drain have used parts of it as a refuse dump, which reduces the capacity of the watercourse and increases the risk of obstruction during heavy rainfall. The Assembly is currently using additional workers and machinery to remove the refuse from the site.

cards.headline: Probe panel recommends suspension of four students following attack on journalists at Rajshahi University, Bangladesh

pages.text: A five-member probe committee at Rajshahi University (RU) in Bangladesh has recommended the suspension of four students following an October 4 attack on journalists at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall. The attack, which occurred while journalists were performing professional duties, resulted in injuries to at least 10 people, including four journalists, according to Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Md Faridul Islam. The university administration received the investigation report around midnight on Thursday, and the Vice-Chancellor presented the findings to journalists on Friday. The committee was originally formed by the university administration to identify those involved in the incident after a meeting with journalists, with the Vice-Chancellor directing a report be submitted within 72 hours. The probe panel recommended the suspension of Ahsan Habib, Vice President of the RU unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD); Hasibul Hasan, Joint General Secretary; Ariful Islam, General Secretary of the Ziaur Rahman Hall Students’ Union; and JCD activist Bishal Chakraborty.

In addition to the recommended suspensions, the committee advised further investigation into allegations against four other students before taking action: Rakibul Islam, assistant cultural affairs secretary of the RU Central Students’ Union (RUCSU); Takbir Ahmed Emon, vice president of the RU unit of JCD; Syed Sajharul Islam, joint general secretary; and JCD activist Tanim Rahman. The committee also recommended issuing warnings to Bulbul Rahman and Shariful Islam, both vice-presidents of the university unit of JCD, and Shahriar Alam, an assistant office secretary.

cards.headline: Iraq rejects Syria's request to repatriate 4,000 suspected ISIS detainees

pages.text: Iraq has rejected a request from Syria to repatriate approximately 4,000 Syrian detainees suspected of links to the Islamic State (ISIS), according to Iraqi National Security Advisor Qasim al-Aboudi. The detainees were transferred from Syrian detention facilities to Iraqi custody earlier this year. Al-Aboudi told The Associated Press that Damascus requested the Syrian nationals be handed over for trial in Syria, but Baghdad declined the request. A recent meeting involving Iraqi, Syrian, and U.S. officials addressed the fate of the detainees. Al-Aboudi stated that hundreds of the Syrians currently held in Iraq are believed to be senior members of ISIS. He noted that Iraq is conducting investigations and that anyone proven to have committed crimes in Iraq will be tried under Iraqi law. Al-Aboudi added that detainees from countries that do not impose the death penalty would not face capital punishment in Iraq, and those convicted could potentially be transferred to their home countries to serve remaining sentences if prisoner-transfer agreements are in place.

Regarding the status of other detainees, al-Aboudi said Iraq has already returned approximately 50 Syrian detainees after determining they were not members of ISIS. Iraqi authorities have also identified about 400 Syrian detainees who were not affiliated with the group and could be released. Additionally, al-Aboudi stated that Baghdad has requested $500 million from the United States and other members of the international coalition against ISIS to assist with detention and prison-security costs. While the coalition has expressed willingness to provide support, Iraq has not yet received the funding. This detainee issue follows the end of the United States' 12-year military mission against ISIS in Iraq, with the final U.S. troops withdrawing from the country at the end of September.

cards.headline: Two Renoir paintings recovered after theft from museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, France

pages.text: Two paintings by French impressionist Pierre-Auguste Renoir have been recovered approximately one month after they were stolen from a museum in southern France, according to the mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer. The recovered works are titled *Portrait of Madame Colonna Romano* (1910) and *Jeune fille au puits* (1886).  The paintings were stolen in September when thieves entered the Renoir Museum by cutting through a fence and smashing a window. The suspects used an electric saw to cut through frame mountings and initially fled with four paintings, though they abandoned two of them in the museum's garden during their escape.  Bryan Masson, the mayor of Cagnes-sur-Mer and a member of France's National Rally, stated that the recovery provides immense relief and noted that the works are part of the city's history and cultural heritage. While the town hall initially planned to provide further details on the recovery on Friday, a planned press conference was cancelled.  Regarding the investigation, a source close to the probe told AFP that five people had been arrested, while the town hall confirmed in a statement that six suspects have been arrested in relation to the heist. No official statement has been released by the police.

cards.headline: Communities oppose waste-to-energy plant near Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: Construction of a $467 million power plant designed to incinerate municipal waste for electricity near Dhaka, Bangladesh, is facing opposition from nearby communities over potential health risks from toxic air pollution, according to a report by Eyamin Sajid for Mongabay. The project, which is being overseen by the Dhaka North City Corporation and owned by the China Machinery Engineering Corporation (CMEC), is slated for completion in December 2028. The facility is intended to incinerate up to 3,000 metric tons of waste daily to generate up to 42.5 megawatts of electricity. Densely populated communities and several schools are located less than a mile from the site. Local farmers, including rice and vegetable grower Md Naim, told Mongabay that unmanaged trash fires at the current dumpsite already cause headaches and breathing difficulties due to smoke and ash.

An environmental impact assessment for the project states the incinerator will produce 74.8 metric tons of airborne fly ash daily. Additionally, an analysis by environmental groups indicates the plant will generate 39.56 metric tons of toxic substances annually, including heavy metals, dioxins, and furans, alongside 73,576 metric tons of solid waste. Hasan Mehedi, secretary of the Bangladesh Working Group on Ecology and Development (BWGED), stated that regular operation of the plant could lead to respiratory and lung-related problems, eye irritation, fatigue, and long-term health issues for local residents, particularly children and the elderly, due to chronic exposure to air pollution.

cards.headline: Separatist sentiment addressed at United Conservative Party annual general meeting in Alberta

pages.text: During the United Conservative Party’s 2025 annual general meeting in Edmonton, Alberta, a member of the party raised the issue of provincial independence. While sitting on stage with her cabinet, Premier Danielle Smith was approached by Jeff Rath, a constitutional lawyer, UCP member, and figure in the Alberta independence movement. Rath asked the room how many members favored a free and independent Alberta, an inquiry that was met with an ovation from the crowd. Smith responded by stating, 'Well, I support an independent Alberta within a united Canada.'
